DURR-FULL:v4p315/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p315/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p315/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God invited even Pharaoh to repentance; no one may make people despair of it, and repentance begins with God's enabling turn toward the servant.
DURR-FULL:v4p315/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: دعا الله إلى توبته من قال (أنا ربكم الأعلى)

DURR-FULL:v4p387/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r2.speaker: جبريل
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r2.claim: Gabriel recounts that Pharaoh had claimed divinity, then stuffed his mouth when drowning threatened, fearing he would receive mercy.
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: قال لي جبريل: ما غضب ربك على أحد

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p542/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p542/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p542/r3.claim: Hāmān held the rank of prime minister or at least a minister responsible for construction and development at Pharaoh’s court.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p542/r3.anchor: he had the same status in the court of the Pharaoh as that of a prime minister or at least a minister of construction and development.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p542/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p542/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p542/r4.claim: The construction phrase can mean making a brick kiln or building a clay structure and firing it; heated mud construction was common in Egypt and Nineveh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p542/r4.anchor: a common way of construction in Nineveh and Egypt was to build a house with mud and then have it heated strongly with flames.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p542/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p542/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p542/r5.claim: The construction wording contains taḍmīn, implying Pharaoh would climb the building and peer at Moses’ God as a mocking gesture.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p542/r5.anchor: Obviously, these words were meant to make fun of Moses (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p543/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p543/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p543/r1.claim: Pharaoh claims there is no god for his people but himself and ridicules Moses’ God; autocrats’ mockery can be mistaken by followers for proof.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p543/r1.anchor: at times, autocrats and tyrants make fun of absolutely evident facts in this way.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p543/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p543/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p543/r2.claim: Pharaoh’s followers may have taken his mockery literally because they regarded him as an avatar of the Sun God; his tower scheme may have deceived the masses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p543/r2.anchor: they regarded the Pharaoh to be an avatar of their Sun God. How could it be difficult for an avatar to take a peep

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p305/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p305/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p305/r6.claim: Pharaoh's denial of knowing another god may deny any other god exists or literally deny his knowledge; his drowning confession shows he lied.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p305/r6.anchor: ونفى فرعون علمه بإله غيره للملأ، ويريد بذلك نفي وجوده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p306/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p306/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p306/r1.claim: Pharaoh tells Haman to heat clay; a report calls him the first brick-maker, and the wording has Pharaoh instructing Haman in an unfamiliar process.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p306/r1.anchor: قيل: وهو أول من عمل الآجر، ولم يقل: اطبخ الآجر، لأنه لم يتقدم لهامان علم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p306/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p306/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p306/r2.claim: Pharaoh pretends the God of Moses can be reached despite knowing this impossible; some rational people may comply from fear of his violence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p306/r2.anchor: أوهم قومه أن إله موسى يمكن الوصول إليه والقدرة عليه، وهو عالم متيقن أن ذلك لا يمكن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p306/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p306/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p306/r3.claim: The order to build a tower does not prove it was built; reports disagree, and اطلع means ascend just like طلع.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p306/r3.anchor: ولا يدل الأمر ببناء الصرح على أنه بني، وقد اختلف في ذلك، فقيل: بناه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh habitually met Moses' proofs with a sophism meant to persuade the ignorant; here he advances two sophisms.
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r1.anchor: كانت عادته متى ظهرت حجة موسى أن يتعلق في دفع تلك الحجة بشبهة يروجها على أغمار قومه

RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r2.speaker: فرعون
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh's first sophism denies any other god because he claims there is no evidence; he says celestial bodies suffice to explain changes in the lower world, so no maker is needed.
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r2.anchor: أما الأول فقد كان اعتماده على أن ما لا دليل عليه لم يجز إثباته

RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r3.claim: The premise that no proof exists is false: proof that bodies originated establishes that the heavens and stars originated, and every originated thing must have an originator, so the world has a maker.
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r3.anchor: لأنا إذا عرفنا بالدليل حدوث الأجسام عرفنا حدوث الأفلاك والكواكب

RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r4.claim: Some deniers turn failure to find evidence after searching into proof of nonexistence; Pharaoh was less extreme because he only withheld affirmation for lack of proof and suspected Moses was lying.
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r4.anchor: فرجع حاصل كلامهم بعد التحقيق إلى أن كل ما لا يعرف عليه دليل وجب نفيه

RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r5.claim: Pharaoh's claim to be a deity did not mean he claimed to create the heavens, earth, seas, mountains, people, or their attributes; deity here means the one worshipped, and he claimed people owed obedience only to their king.
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r5.anchor: بل الإله هو المعبود فالرجل كان ينفي الصانع ويقول لا تكليف على الناس إلا أن يطيعوا ملكهم وينقادوا لأمره

RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r6.claim: Against the common reading that Pharaoh claimed to create heaven and earth, al-Razi says Pharaoh knew God and made the claim to mislead the gullible, as he argued in his commentary on 20:49.
RAZI-FULL:v24p215#2/r6.anchor: على أنه كان عارفا بالله تعالى وأنه كان يقول ذلك ترويجا على الأغمار

RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r1.speaker: المشبهة
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r1.claim: The anthropomorphists cite this verse to argue that God is in heaven; al-Razi replies that Moses called God Lord of heaven and earth without restricting Him to heaven, and Pharaoh maliciously distorted this.
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r1.anchor: تعلقت المشبهة بهذه الآية في أن الله تعالى في السماء قالوا لولا أن موسى عليه السلام دعاه إلى ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r2.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r2.claim: One account says Pharaoh built the tower: Haman assembled fifty thousand builders, besides laborers and attendants, to make bricks, plaster, timber, and nails, raising a structure higher than any before it.
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r2.anchor: فال قوم إنه بناه قالوا إنه لما أمر ببناء الصرح جمع هامان العمال حتى اجتمع خمسون ألف بناء سوى الأتباع والأجراء

RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r3.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r3.claim: In that account Gabriel struck the tower at sunset and broke it into three pieces; one fell on Pharaoh's army and killed a million men, another into the sea, and another in the west, killing all the workers.
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r3.anchor: فبعث الله تعالى جبريل عليه السلام عند غروب الشمس فضربه بجناحه فقطعه ثلاث قطع قطعة وقعت على عسكر فرعون فقتلت ألف ألف رجل

RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r4.claim: A further story says Pharaoh climbed the tower and shot an arrow toward heaven; it returned stained with blood, so he claimed to have killed Moses' God, after which Gabriel was sent to destroy the tower.
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r4.anchor: ويروى في هذه القصة أن فرعون ارتقى فوقه ورمى بنشابة نحو السماء فأراد الله أن يفتنهم فردت إليهم وهي ملطوخة بالدم

RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r5.speaker: ومن الناس
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r5.claim: Others say the tower was never built: rational people know climbing a tower cannot bring them nearer to heaven, since a person on a high mountain sees the sky as from the ground; an arrow cannot reach it either.
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r5.anchor: ومن الناس من قال إنه لم يبن ذلك الصرح لأنه يبعد من العقلاء أن يظنوا أنهم بصعود الصرح يقربون من السماء مع علمهم بأن من على أعلى الجبال الشاهقة يرى السماء

RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r6.claim: Al-Razi rejects a literal account that violates necessary reason, since it would give attackers a strong pretext to disparage the Quran.

RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r7.claim: Al-Razi prefers that Pharaoh only pretended to build the tower, or that the order continued his claim that no proof of a maker exists: reason cannot prove it, nor can the senses without ascending heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r7.anchor: فالأقرب أنه كان أوهم البناء ولم يبن أو كان هذا من تتمة قوله

RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r8.claim: On al-Razi's preferred reading, Pharaoh's tower order was mockery: after declaring that neither reason nor sensation could establish a creator, he concludes that Moses is a liar.
RAZI-FULL:v24p216/r8.anchor: وإنما قال ذلك على سبيل التهكم فبمجموع هذه الأشياء قرر أنه لا دليل على الصانع

RAZI-FULL:v24p217/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p217/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p217/r1.claim: Pharaoh says to fire clay rather than simply to make bricks because he was the first brickmaker and knew the craft; the phrasing also suits Quranic eloquence and the speech of tyrants.
RAZI-FULL:v24p217/r1.anchor: ولم يقل اطبخ لي الآجر واتخذه لأنه أول من عمل الآجر فهو يعلمه الصنعة ولأن هذه العبارة أليق بفصاحة القرآن وأشبه بكلام الجبابرة

RAZI-FULL:v24p217/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p217/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p217/r2.claim: Calling his minister Haman by name in the middle of the speech displays Pharaoh's self-exaltation and tyranny.
RAZI-FULL:v24p217/r2.anchor: بالإيقاد على الطين فنادى باسمه بيافي وسط الكلام دليل على التعظم والتجبر

RAZI-FULL:v24p217/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p217/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p217/r3.claim: The verbs ṭalaʿa and iṭṭalaʿ can both mean to ascend; one says either of ascending a mountain.
RAZI-FULL:v24p217/r3.anchor: والطلوع والاطلاع الصعود يقال طلع الجبل واطلع بمعنى واحد

BURSEVI:v6p294#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p294#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p294#2/r6.claim: Pharaoh spoke after gathering the magicians and preparing to challenge Moses.

BURSEVI:v6p294#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p294#2/r7.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v6p294#2/r7.claim: One report places forty years between Pharaoh's claim that he knew no god for them and his later claim to be their highest lord.

BURSEVI:v6p294#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p294#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p294#2/r8.claim: Pharaoh meant that no god other than himself existed on earth, while Moses affirmed another God, creator of the heavens.
BURSEVI:v6p294#2/r8.anchor: أي ليس لكم إله غيري في الأرض

BURSEVI:v6p295/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p295/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p295/r1.claim: The clay means earth mixed with water; Pharaoh orders bricks to be made, and he is said to be the first to make bricks.
BURSEVI:v6p295/r1.anchor: هو التراب والماء المختلط أي اصنع لي آجرا :

BURSEVI:v6p295/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p295/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p295/r2.claim: Saying to fire up clay rather than simply to cook bricks implicitly teaches the brickmaking craft.
BURSEVI:v6p295/r2.anchor: ولذلك أمر باتخاذه على وجه يتضمن تعليم الصنعة حيث لم يقل اطبخ لي الآجر

BURSEVI:v6p295/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p295/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p295/r3.claim: A sarḥ is a lofty, prominent palace, like a pillar or minaret.

BURSEVI:v6p295/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p295/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p295/r4.claim: Pharaoh says he will look at Moses' God and reach a position above him.

BURSEVI:v6p295/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p295/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p295/r5.claim: Pharaoh calls Moses a liar about having a God other than Pharaoh and about being God's messenger, but does so to deceive his people, not from conviction.
BURSEVI:v6p295/r5.anchor: في ادعائه أن له إلها غيري وأنه رسوله قاله تلبيسا وتمويها على قومه لا تحقيقا

BURSEVI:v6p295/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p295/r6.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v6p295/r6.claim: The Questions Raised Against the Qur'an says Pharaoh knew his own needs and afflictions made him unfit for divinity; his claim was defiant denial, not inward belief.

BURSEVI:v6p295/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p295/r7.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p295/r7.claim: Kashifi says Pharaoh imagined God as a body located in heaven and thought it possible to ascend to him.

BURSEVI:v6p295/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p295/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p295/r8.claim: The Persian verses reject locating God: the maker of place cannot itself occupy place, and neither place nor time reaches or describes God.
BURSEVI:v6p295/r8.anchor: كه مكان آفرين مكان ه كند آسمان كر بر آسمان ه كند نه مكان ره برد برو نه زمان

BURSEVI:v6p295/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p295/r9.speaker: صاحب كشاف
BURSEVI:v6p295/r9.claim: Al-Kashshaf reports that Haman assembled many master craftsmen and workers to bake bricks and construct the palace, burdening Moses and Aaron because the Israelites were tormented in its building.
BURSEVI:v6p295/r9.anchor: صاحب كشاف : (آورده كه هامان ملعون ناه هزار استاد جمع كرد

BURSEVI:v6p295/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p295/r10.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v6p295/r10.claim: Abu al-Layth says the palace used glass cullet mortar, was dangerously tall in wind, and measured 5,000 cubits high by 3,000 wide.
BURSEVI:v6p295/r10.anchor: قال أبو الليث : كان ملاط القصر خبث القوارير وكان الرجل

STUDYQURAN:28:38/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r1.claim: Pharaoh’s claim is compared with his later declaration that he is the most high lord.
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r1.anchor: See also 79:24, where Pharaoh says: I am your lord most high

STUDYQURAN:28:38/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r2.claim: The source does not establish whether the tower was ever begun or built.
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r2.anchor: It is not known whether the tower was ever actually begun or built (R).

STUDYQURAN:28:38/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r3.speaker: some traditions
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r3.claim: Some traditions say Pharaoh built the tower, climbed it, and shot an arrow skyward, which fell back and struck him, drawing blood; no grading is stated.
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r3.anchor: Some traditions exist that Pharaoh actually had such a structure built, climbed to the top, and shot an arrow toward the sky

STUDYQURAN:28:38/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r4.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī calls these reports not sane, questioning how a structure taller than a mountain could be built and a weapon used from its top.
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r4.anchor: al-Rāzī finds such accounts to be

STUDYQURAN:28:38/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r5.claim: The order to build may be Pharaoh’s rhetorical move, perhaps delivered ironically; compare 40:36–37.
STUDYQURAN:28:38/r5.anchor: The order to build it can be seen as a kind of rhetorical move on Pharaoh’s part, perhaps said with a sense of irony

TAB-FULL:v18p254/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r1.claim: Pharaoh tells his nobles that he knows no deity besides himself for them to worship, denying Moses’ claim that they have another lord and object of worship.
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r1.anchor: فتعبدوه، وتصدقوا قول موسى فيما جاءكم به من أن لكم وله ربا غيري ومعبودا سواي

TAB-FULL:v18p254/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r2.claim: Pharaoh asks Haman to make bricks by firing clay.
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r2.anchor: يقول: فاعمل لي آجرا، وذكر أنه أول من طبخ الآجر وبنى به

TAB-FULL:v18p254/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r3.claim: Mujāhid explains the clay as molded earth made into fired brick.
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين} [القصص: 38] قال: على المدر يكون لبنا مطبوخا

TAB-FULL:v18p254/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Pharaoh was the first to order brickmaking and build with bricks.
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r4.anchor: قال ابن جريج: «أول من أمر بصنعة الآجر وبنى به فرعون»

TAB-FULL:v18p254/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r5.claim: Qatāda says Pharaoh was the first to fire bricks for building the tower.
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: " {فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين} [القصص: 38] قال: فكان أول من طبخ الآجر يبني به الصرح

TAB-FULL:v18p254/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the fired building material is clay used to construct buildings.
TAB-FULL:v18p254/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قول الله: " {فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين} [القصص: 38] قال: المطبوخ الذي يوقد عليه

TAB-FULL:v18p255/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r1.claim: A “ṣarḥ” is a raised, level building, like a palace; an anonymous poem uses the plural “ṣurūḥ.”
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r1.anchor: يقول: ابن لي بالآجر بناء، وكل بناء مسطح فهو صرح كالقصر

TAB-FULL:v18p255/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r2.claim: The poetic form “ṣurūḥ” is the plural of “ṣarḥ.”
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r2.anchor: يحسِب أعلامهن الصروحا يعني بالصروح: جمع صرح

TAB-FULL:v18p255/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r3.claim: Pharaoh says he will look upon the deity Moses worships and calls people to worship.
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r3.anchor: انظر إلى معبود موسى، الذي يعبده، ويدعو إلى عبادته

TAB-FULL:v18p255/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r4.claim: Pharaoh calls Moses a liar about a deity in heaven who supports and sends him; al-Ṭabarī cites the same accusation in 7:66.
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r4.anchor: من أن له معبودا يعبده في السماء، وأنه هو الذي يؤيده وينصره

TAB-FULL:v18p255/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r5.claim: Al-Suddī reports that after the tower was built, Pharaoh climbed it, shot an arrow toward heaven, received it back bloodied, and claimed he had killed Moses’ God; God is exalted above their claim.
TAB-FULL:v18p255/r5.anchor: عن السدي، قال: قال فرعون لقومه: {يا أيها الملأ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري، فأوقد لي يا هامان

TABATABAI:28:37-38/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:37-38/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:37-38/r7.claim: Pharaoh insinuates that Moses’ call and miraculous signs have not convinced him of God’s existence or shown the signs to be divine proofs.
TABATABAI:28:37-38/r7.anchor: فيه تعريض لموسى بما جاء به من الدعوة الحقة المؤيدة بالآيات المعجزة يريد أنه لم يتبين له حقية ما يدعو إليه موسى

TABATABAI:28:38/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:38/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:38/r1.claim: Pharaoh casts his claim as fair-minded reasoning so the elite will accept it, as in his other claim that he shows them only what he sees and guides them only to the right path.
TABATABAI:28:38/r1.anchor: فقوله { ما علمت لكم من إله غيري } سوق للكلام في صورة الإنصاف ليقع في قلوب الملأ موقع القبول

TABATABAI:28:38/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:38/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:38/r2.claim: The statement is a counter-restriction: Moses affirms God’s divinity and denies it of all others, while Pharaoh denies God and claims divinity for himself; other gods worshipped by Pharaoh’s people are not addressed.
TABATABAI:28:38/r2.anchor: قصر القلب فقد كان موسى عليه السلام يثبت الألوهية لله سبحانه وينفيها عن غيره وهو ينفيها عنه تعالى

TABATABAI:28:38/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:38/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:38/r3.claim: Kindle fire over clay means firing it into bricks for building; a ṣarḥ is a high, exposed structure, from the idea of something becoming visible.
TABATABAI:28:38/r3.anchor: والصرح البناء العالي المكشوف من صرح الشيء إذا ظهر ففي الجملة أمر باتخاذ الآجر

TABATABAI:28:38/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:38/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:38/r4.claim: The result is put before its premise: Pharaoh wants a structure to climb high enough to look toward the sky and perhaps see Moses’ God, whom he imagines as a body somewhere in the atmosphere or celestial spheres.
TABATABAI:28:38/r4.anchor: والكلام من وضع النتيجة موضع المقدمة والتقدير اجعل لي صرحا أصعد إلى أعلى درجاته

TABATABAI:28:38/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:38/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:38/r5.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh’s claim may be deliberate obfuscation meant to mislead the people.
TABATABAI:28:38/r5.anchor: أو كان هذا القول من قبيل التعمية على الناس وإضلالهم

TABATABAI:28:38/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:38/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:38/r6.claim: Another possibility is that Pharaoh wants an observatory to watch the stars and see whether they indicate a messenger’s mission or the truth of Moses’ description; a parallel wording supports it.
TABATABAI:28:38/r6.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون المراد أن يبني له رصدا يترصد الكواكب

TABATABAI:28:38/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:38/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:38/r7.claim: Pharaoh escalates from ignorance implied by “I know no god but myself” to suspicion that Moses is lying, which Tabataba’i says is itself a lie intended to confuse the people.
TABATABAI:28:38/r7.anchor: وقوله { وإني لأظنه من الكاذبين } ترق منه من الجهل

TABATABAI:28:38-42/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:38-42/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:28:38-42/r1.claim: Some commentators read this as denying a god through lack of knowledge, implying that a real god would have become evident; Tabataba’i rejects this because it does not fit the verse’s ending.
TABATABAI:28:38-42/r1.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن قوله { ما علمت لكم من إله غيري } من قبيل نفي المعلوم بنفي العلم فيما لو كان لبان

TABATABAI:28:38-42/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:38-42/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:38-42/r2.claim: Moses counters Pharaoh’s false denial by saying he already knows these signs were sent only by the Lord of the heavens and earth.
TABATABAI:28:38-42/r2.anchor: لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب السماوات والأرض

THALABI:v7p250/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p250/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p250/r5.claim: Pharaoh orders Haman to fire clay and make bricks for him.
THALABI:v7p250/r5.anchor: فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين فاطبخ لي الآجر

THALABI:v7p250/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p250/r6.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p250/r6.claim: Some say Pharaoh was the first to make bricks and build with them.
THALABI:v7p250/r6.anchor: وقيل: إنه أول من اتخذ الآجر وبنى به.

THALABI:v7p250/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p250/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
THALABI:v7p250/r7.claim: Exegetes report that Haman gathered fifty thousand builders plus supporting workers, raised a tower higher than any human construction since creation, and Pharaoh tested it by shooting an arrow skyward; it returned stained with blood.
THALABI:v7p250/r7.anchor: جمع هامان العمال والفعلة حتى اجتمع خمسون ألف بناء سوى الأتباع والأجراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r1.speaker: مقاتل وقتادة وأبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r1.claim: They explain the order as firing clay to make bricks; Muqatil and Qatada say Pharaoh was the first to bake bricks.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: يقول: أوقد النار على الطين، حتى يصير اللبن آجرا. وكان فرعون أول من طبخ الآجر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r2.claim: They define a sarh as a tall, high, elevated palace.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r2.anchor: يعني: قصرا طويلا عاليا مرتفعا. قاله ابن عباس والمفسرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r3.claim: Al-Wahidi notes that he has already explained the word sarh in his commentary on Surat al-Naml.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r3.anchor: وتفسير الصرح مذكور في سورة: النمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the verb as “I will climb up to him.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r4.anchor: {لعلي أطلع إلى إله موسى} قال ابن عباس: أصعد إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r5.claim: Pharaoh tries to mislead people into thinking Moses’ God needs a location and direction, since he speaks of climbing up to Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r5.anchor: وهذا إيهام من فرعون للناس أن الذي يدعوه إليه موسى يجري مجراه في الحاجة إلى المكان والجهة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq says Pharaoh admits uncertainty rather than certainty that Moses is lying, showing he rejected Moses without being certain he was not a prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: قد اعترف بأنه شاك لم يتيقن أن موسى كاذب. وفي هذا بيان أنه كفر بموسى على غير تيقن أنه ليس بنبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r7.claim: Muqatil says Pharaoh accused Moses of lying about there being a God in heaven.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يقول: إني لأحسب موسى من الكاذبين فيما يقول: إن في السماء إلها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r8.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r8.claim: Al-Kalbi says Pharaoh claimed Moses was lying because nothing exists in heaven; al-Wahidi says this view and Muqatil’s imply anthropomorphism and direction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p398/r8.anchor: قال الكلبي: يقول: إني لأظن موسى كاذبا، ما في السماء من شيء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:37-38/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:37-38/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:37-38/r3.claim: Pharaoh orders Haman to bake bricks from clay.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:37-38/r3.anchor: فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين } أي: اطبخ لي الآجر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:37-38/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:37-38/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:37-38/r4.claim: A ṣarḥ is a tall, elevated building.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:37-38/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:37-38/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:37-38/r5.claim: Pharaoh says he wants to look at and stand above Moses’ God.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r3.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r3.claim: In al-Ḥasan’s interpretation, Pharaoh deliberately lies when he claims to know no god for the people besides himself.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r3.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {وقال فرعون يأيها الملأ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري} [القصص: 38] تعمد الكذب، في تفسير الحسن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r4.claim: Pharaoh orders clay fired into bricks; the source says this was the first brickmaking.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r4.anchor: {فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين} [القصص: 38] ، أي: فاطبخ لي آجرا فكان أول ما عمل الآجر.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r5.claim: The command means “build me a lofty structure.”
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r5.anchor: {فاجعل لي صرحا} [القصص: 38] ، أي: فابن لي صرحا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r6.claim: Pharaoh had a high tower built, already knew Moses was God’s messenger, and lied in claiming he would seek Moses’ god.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r6.anchor: {لعلي أطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه من الكاذبين} [القصص: 38] فبنى له صرحا عاليا، وقد علم فرعون أن موسى رسول الله، وهذا القول منه كذب.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r7.claim: Pharaoh’s knowing denial is illustrated by the statement that people rejected the signs while inwardly certain of them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r7.anchor: قال الله عز وجل: {وجحدوا بها واستيقنتها أنفسهم ظلما وعلوا} [النمل: 14]

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r8.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r8.claim: Qatāda says denial occurs only after knowledge.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p593/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: والجحد لا يكون إلا من بعد المعرفة.

ELMALILI:28:38/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:38/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:38/r1.claim: Al-malaʾ addresses the people, specifically a conspicuous, impressive gathering.
ELMALILI:28:38/r1.anchor: ey millet: ey şu gözler dolduran cemaat

ELMALILI:28:38/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:38/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:38/r2.claim: Elmalili frames Pharaoh’s address as the act of a tyrant summoning his community.
ELMALILI:28:38/r2.anchor: Firavun ise -bak ne zâlim, cemiyetini toplayıp da- dedi ki

ELMALILI:28:38/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:38/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:38/r3.claim: Pharaoh knows he did not create his people and has a creator himself, yet denies God’s exclusive right to divinity and wrongs the concepts of creation and godhood.
ELMALILI:28:38/r3.anchor: Pekâlâ bilir ki şu halkı yaratan kendisi değildir, kendisini de bir yaratan vardır.

ELMALILI:28:38/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:38/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:38/r4.claim: He presents lawmaking and government as his own will with no higher authority, demanding that people obey, love, fear, and worship him.
ELMALILI:28:38/r4.anchor: ne irade ederse olurmuş, hükm ü hükûmetini nakzedebilecek mâfevk bir kuvvet yokmuş gibi gösteriyor.

ELMALILI:28:38/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:38/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:38/r5.claim: By saying “I know of no other god” rather than “there is none,” Pharaoh tries to appear fair-minded.
ELMALILI:28:38/r5.anchor: İlk önce “yoktur” demiyor, “bilmiyorum” diye insaflı görünmek istiyor

ELMALILI:28:38/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:38/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:38/r6.claim: Pharaoh insinuates that the Lord of heaven and earth is a physical object that could be seen by surveying the sky, using a scientific-sounding ruse against the people.
ELMALILI:28:38/r6.anchor: göklerin yerin rabbi güya semâyı rasad etmekle görünmesi lâzım gelen bir cisim ve cismânî imiş gibi tevehhüm ettirerek halka karşı ilm ü fen yolundan bir desîse

ELMALILI:28:38/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:38/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:38/r7.claim: The command means to fire clay in a kiln for making bricks; it does not explicitly say “bake bricks.”
ELMALILI:28:38/r7.anchor: “tuğla pişir” demeyip bu tâbiri kullanması, kerpici pişirip tuğla yapmayı

ELMALILI:28:38/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:38/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:38/r8.claim: A reported explanation says Pharaoh first conceived the craft of making fired bricks and thereby taught the technique.
ELMALILI:28:38/r8.anchor: kerpici pişirip tuğla yapmayı ibtidâ Firavun düşünmüş olduğundan bu suretle sanatı tâlim eylemiş deniliyor.

ELMALILI:28:38/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:38/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:38/r9.claim: A ṣarḥ is a tall tower built as an observation post to survey the heavens.
ELMALILI:28:38/r9.anchor: Hemen bana bir kule yap semâyı tarassud edecek bir rasad kulesi binâ et

ELMALILI:28:38/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:38/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:38/r10.claim: Though he considers Moses a liar, Pharaoh pretends to conduct an empirical search to expose him and even to confront Moses’s God if found.
ELMALILI:28:38/r10.anchor: her ihtimâle karşı güya ilm ü fen dairesinde bilfiil taharriyât yaparak o yalanı meydana çıkaracak ve şayet onun ilâhını bulursa güya onun da hakkından gelecek imiş gibi görünmek istiyor.

ELMALILI:28:38/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:38/r11.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:28:38/r11.claim: Some say Pharaoh’s statement remained empty talk and that trying to reach the sky with such a tower is irrational.
ELMALILI:28:38/r11.anchor: Bazıları bunun sade bir laftan ibaret kaldığını ve öyle bir kule ile göğe çıkmaya çalışmanın gayr-i ma‘kūl olduğunu söylemişlerse

ELMALILI:28:38/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:38/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:38/r12.claim: Other accounts report that the tower was built and later collapsed.
ELMALILI:28:38/r12.anchor: diğer taraftan böyle bir kulenin yapılıp yıkıldığını nakletmişlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:38/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:38/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:38/r1.claim: Egyptians treated pharaohs as divine sons and worshipped them; Moses’s Pharaoh saw himself as the greatest god and mockingly ordered Haman to build a tower from which he might see Moses’s God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:38/r1.anchor: Firavunlar Mısır halkı tarafından tanrının oğlu, dolayısıyla tanrı kabul edildiği ve kendisine tapınılma derecesinde yüceltildiği için Mûsâ’nın muhatabı olan Firavun da kendisini “en büyük Tanrı” olarak görmüş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:38/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:38/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:38/r2.claim: Despite many calamities, Pharaoh refused to see or accept the truth; Moses then led Israel toward the Red Sea by God’s command, crossed when it miraculously opened, and Pharaoh and his pursuing army drowned.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:38/r2.anchor: Bir mûcize sonucu denizin yol vermesiyle Mûsâ ve İsrâiloğulları karşıya geçerken, aynı yoldan geçmeye çalışan Firavun, ordusuyla birlikte denize gömüldü

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:38/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:38/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:38/r3.claim: Pharaoh believed in God while drowning, but faith at the point of despair was not accepted.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:38/r3.anchor: Firavun denizde boğulmak üzere iken Allah’a iman etmiş, fakat yeis halindeki imanı kabul edilmemiştir

BAQILLANI:v1p52/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r6.claim: If the eloquent Arabs had regarded the Quran as poetry, they would have challenged it at once, since poetry was easy for them and they had extraordinary control of it.
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r6.anchor: الفصحاء منهم حين أورد عليهم القرآن لو كانوا يعتقدونه شعرا

BAQILLANI:v1p52/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r7.claim: Their failure to exploit poetry despite their urgent motive to discredit the Quran shows they did not see it as poetry; later critics cannot plausibly have noticed what all those eloquent contemporaries missed.
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r7.anchor: علم أنهم لم يعتقدوا فيه شيئا مما يقدره الضعفاء

BURHAN:v3p27/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.claim: Repeated tellings of Moses and Pharaoh differ in wording, order, and detail because each version carries a nuance found only there; unlike earlier scripture's separate single tellings, Joseph's story is collected in one sura.
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.anchor: فقد يوجد في ألفاظها زيادة ونقصان وتقديم وتأخير

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r1.claim: The poem’s categorical claim that the beloved is the sun makes her celestial abode proof that reaching her is impossible, presenting the fact itself rather than an explicit simile.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r1.anchor: ألا تراه كأنه يقول للنفس ما وجه الطمع في الوصول وقد علمت أن حديثك مع الشمس

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r2.claim: Ibn Abi ʿUyaynah’s poem does not deny the comparison: it says she is the sun, then contrasts the nearness of its light with the difficulty of reaching it.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r2.anchor: بيت ابن أبي عيينه في أن لم ينصرف عن التشبيه جملة ولم يبرز في صورة الجاحد له

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r3.claim: Bashshar and al-Mutanabbi state their comparisons openly, respectively likening the beloved to a distant moon and to the sun whose rays approach but cannot be grasped.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r3.anchor: كبيت بشار الذي صرح فيه بالتشبيه وهو ( أو كبدر السماء غير قريب حين يوفى والضوء فيه اقتراب )

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r4.claim: Although mentioning the sun conventionally suggests beauty, in these examples the direct aim is to explain nearness in one respect and distance in another; beauty is only a customary secondary implication.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p267/r4.anchor: يقصد فيها إلى بيان أمر غير الحسن يصير كالشىء الذي يعقل من طريق العرف وعلى سبيل التبع

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p333#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p333#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p333#4/r1.claim: The command is to make fired bricks from clay.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p333#4/r1.anchor: {فأوقد لي ياهامان على الطين} أي اصنع لي الآجر.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p333#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p333#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p333#4/r2.claim: A ṣarḥ is a tall palace.

ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r1.claim: The command means to make fired bricks; a report says Pharaoh was first to make bricks.
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r1.anchor: ويقال إن فرعون أول من عمل الآجر

ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r2.claim: A ṣarḥ is a broad, lofty building.

ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r3.claim: Pharaoh thought his tower might reach the sky so he could see it and whatever was in it.
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r3.anchor: وظن فرعون أنه يتهيأ له أن يبلغ بصرحه نحو السماء

ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r4.claim: ظن can denote doubt or certainty.
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r4.anchor: الظن في اللغة ضرب يكون شكا ويقينا

ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r5.claim: Pharaoh admits uncertainty: he rejected Moses without certainty he lied, though signs made him suspect Moses was a prophet.
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r5.anchor: اعتراف بأنه شاو، وأنه لم يتيقن أن موسى كاذب

ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r6.claim: Pharaoh's statement elsewhere that he knew God sent the signs proves decisive evidence had confronted him.
ZAJJAJ:v4p145/r6.anchor: لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب السماوات والأرض بصائر

ASAD-NOTES:28:37#n36/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:37#n36/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:37#n36/r1.claim: Pharaoh's assertion is not literal: although Egyptians worshipped many gods, Pharaoh was regarded as divine incarnation and received adoration as Lord All-Highest.
ASAD-NOTES:28:37#n36/r1.anchor: ancient Egyptians worshipped many gods, this observation is not to be taken literally

ASAD-NOTES:28:37#n37/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:37#n37/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:37#n37/r1.claim: As an alternative, ittali'u can mean to ascend to the god of Moses.
ASAD-NOTES:28:37#n37/r1.anchor: Or: "ascend to the god of Moses".

ASAD-NOTES:28:37#n37/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:37#n37/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:37#n37/r2.claim: The lofty tower evokes pyramid building and derisively mocks Moses' conception of God as an all-embracing power beyond all existence.
ASAD-NOTES:28:37#n37/r2.anchor: a derisory, contemptuous reference to Moses' concept of God as an all-embracing Power, inconceivably high above all that exists

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r1.claim: In al-Qasas, fear prevents Moses from speaking with certainty about what he will do; al-Naml omits fear and uses a confident declaration.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r1.anchor: القصص لم يدعه يقطع بالأمر فإن الخائف لا يستطيع القطع بما سيفعل بخلاف الآمن. ولما لم يذكر الخوف في سورة النمل بناه على الوثوق والقطع بالأمر.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r2.claim: The wording used in al-Naml suits the honor shown to Moses, unlike the wording in al-Qasas.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r2.anchor: إن ما ذكره في النمل هو المناسب لمقام التكريم لموسى بخلاف ما في القصص.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r3.claim: Al-Qasas has ten expressions of hope, whereas al-Naml has only two; this contrast makes hope characteristic of al-Qasas and certainty characteristic of al-Naml.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r3.anchor: وهذا كله ترجٍّ. وذلك في عشرة مواطن في حين لم يَرِد الترجي في سورة النمل إلا في موطنين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r4.claim: Al-Naml repeatedly uses certainty, as shown by the hoopoe's certain report and two confident promises to bring the throne.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p94/r4.anchor: أَحَطتُ بِمَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ وَجِئْتُكَ مِن سَبَإٍ بِنَبَإٍ يَقِينٍ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r1.claim: Al-Qasas uses expressions of hope in ten places, while al-Naml has only two; the author says hope marks al-Qasas and certainty marks al-Naml.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r1.anchor: الترجي من سمات سورة القصص، والقطع من سمات سورة النمل

IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.claim: Of twelve disputed possessive yāʾs, Nafi opens all except معي ردءا, which he leaves quiescent.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا قوله ﴿ معي ردءا ﴾ فإنه أسكنها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr open nine listed possessive yāʾs and leave quiescent إني أريد, ستجدني إن شاء الله, and معي ردءا.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.anchor: وفتح ابن كثير تسع آيات منهن وأسكن ﴿ إني أريد ﴾ و ﴿ ستجدني إن شاء الله ﴾

QIRAAT-ER:28:38:24#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:38:24#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:38:24#1/r1.claim: The explicit final yāʾ with fatḥa realizes the first-person suffix without changing its root, meaning, or parsing.
QIRAAT-ER:28:38:24#1/r1.anchor: Variant spells out the 1cs pronoun ya explicitly (fatḥah on final yāʾ instead of elision/sukūn)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p91#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p91#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p91#3/r1.claim: Qatāda says he had heard that Pharaoh was the first to bake bricks.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p91#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين ﴾ قال بلغني أنه أول من طبخ الآجر

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r1.claim: Pharaoh denies knowing of another god for his people rather than directly denying another god's existence; ignorance alone does not prove nonexistence.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r1.anchor: والظاهر أنه أراد حقيقة ما يدل عليه كلامه وهو نفي علمه باله غيره دون وجوده فان عدم العلم بالشيء لا يدل على عدمه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r2.claim: Moses had told Pharaoh that he knew the Lord of the heavens and earth had sent the signs, showing Pharaoh knew their God was other than himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r2.anchor: لأن ظاهر قول موسى عليه السلام له لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب السموات والأرض بصائر

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r3.claim: Pharaoh chose this wording to seem fair-minded and make his people receptive to later claims about God, as a satanic stratagem.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r3.anchor: وما تركه أوفق ظاهرا بما قصده من تبعيد قومه عن اتباع موسى عليه السلام اختيارا لدسيسة شيطانية وهو إظهار أنه منصف في الجملة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r4.claim: The command means to fire clay into bricks, distinguishing it from simply saying to manufacture bricks.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r4.anchor: أي اصنع لي آجرا فاجعل لي منه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r5.claim: A ṣarḥ is a high, open structure, from the sense of something becoming visible.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r5.anchor: أي بناء مكشوفا عاليا من صرح الشيء إذا ظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r6.claim: Here iṭṭalaʿa means ascend or climb; its iftiʿāl form is used with the bare verb's meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r6.anchor: أي اطلع وأصعد فافتعل بمعنى الفعل المجرد كما في البحر وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r7.claim: Pharaoh insinuates that Moses's God would be a body in the sky that people could climb to.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r7.anchor: كأنه يوهم قومه أنه تعالى لو كان كما يقول موسى لكان جسما في السماء كون الاجسام فيها يمكن الرقي اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r8.claim: Calling Moses a liar reinforces Pharaoh's pose; talk of ascending does not prove he sincerely believes God is located there.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r8.anchor: تأكيدا لما أراد وإعلاما بأن ترجيه الصعود إلى إله موسى عليه السلام ليس لأنه جازم بأنه هناك

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r9.claim: One view says Pharaoh built the tower; reports differ about what he did after its construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r9.anchor: والأمر بجعل الصرح وبنائه لا يدل على أنه بني وقد اختلف في ذلك فقيل بناه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r10.claim: If built, Pharaoh may have climbed it with or without a confidant, then falsely claimed to have verified that Moses was lying.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r10.anchor: وعلى الاول يحتمل أن يكون صعد الصرح وحده أو مع من يأمنه على سره وبقي ما بقي ثم نزل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r11.claim: Another view says no tower was built: the order deceived people into thinking he would investigate, so he could claim verification by another method.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r11.anchor: وقيل لم يبن وعلى هذا يكون قوله ذلك وأمره للتلبيس على قومه وإيهامه إياهم أنه بصدد تحقيق الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r12.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r12.claim: Al-Suddī reports Pharaoh climbed the tower, shot an arrow skyward, received it back bloodied, and said he killed Moses's God; al-Ālūsī doubts the report and says it would be mockery if true.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r12.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن السدي قال : لما بني له الصرح ارتقى فوقه فأمر بنشابة فرمى بها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r13.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the people were extraordinarily ignorant for accepting such nonsense, though God grants distinctive qualities to times, places, and people.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r13.anchor: فالقوم كانوا في غاية الغباوة والجهل وإفراط العماية والبلادة وإلا لما نفق عليهم مثل هذا الهذيان

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r14.claim: Some intelligent people may have recognized the bluff but concealed their view from desire for favors or fear of violence.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r14.anchor: كان فيهم من ذوي العقول من يعلم تمويهه وتلبيسه ويعتقد هذيانه فيما يقول إلا أنه نظم نفسه في سلك الجهال

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r15.claim: Al-Ālūsī links this to Pharaoh's later threat to imprison Moses if he took another god, after declaring none but himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r15.anchor: وكان قول اللعين لموسى عليه السلام لئن اتخذت إلها غيري لأجعلنك من المسجونين بعد هذا القول المحكي ههنا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r16.claim: A first alternative says Pharaoh denied knowledge, not existence, and meant Moses lied about being God's messenger; the tower would show the supposed impossibility of reaching God in heaven.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r16.anchor: نفي العلم دون الوجود كما في ذلك الوجه إلا أنه لم ينف الوجود لأنه لم يكن عنده ما يقتضي الجزم بالعدم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r17.claim: On this alternative, Pharaoh reasoned a messenger could not come from a God in heaven if a human could not ascend; the request also mocks.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p80/r17.anchor: لاظهار عدم امكان الصعود الموقوف عليه صحة دعوى الرسالة في زعمه ولعل للتهكم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r1.claim: A second alternative says Pharaoh wanted a high observatory to watch stars for signs of whether God sent Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r1.anchor: أراد بقوله يا هامان الخ طلب أن يجعل له ما يزيل به شكه في الرسالة وذلك بأن يبني له رصدا في موضع عال يرصد منه أحوال الكواكب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r2.claim: This reading must supply a noun and take ilā as ʿalā, inspecting God's judgment through stars; al-Ālūsī finds it strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r2.anchor: إلا أن يراد فأطلع على حكم إله موسى بأوضاع الكواكب والنظر فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r3.claim: A proposal takes Moses's god as the stars or their judgment about his mission; al-Ālūsī says this should not be entertained.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r3.anchor: وجوز على هذا الوجه أن يكون قد أراد باله موسى الكواكب فكأنه قال لعلي أصعد إلى الكواكب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r4.speaker: دريد بن الصمة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r4.claim: The third alternative reads ẓann as certainty, supported by Duraid ibn al-Ṣimma's line.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r4.anchor: ويفسر الظن باليقين كما في قول دريد بن الصمة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r5.claim: On the third alternative, Pharaoh's denial of knowledge means denial of another god's existence, and he certainly considers Moses a liar.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r5.anchor: الثالث أنه أراد بنفي علمه باله غيره نفي وجوده وبظنه كاذبا ظنه كاذبا في إثباته الها غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r6.claim: Some reconcile the statements as public deception followed by a private agreement with Hāmān, but al-Ālūsī says the flow and fa do not support this.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers reading the tower request as mockery: Pharaoh sarcastically repeats Moses's claim that God is in heaven, as when one ironically offers to visit an absent person.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81/r7.anchor: طلبه بناء الصرح بناء على هذا لا يكون منافيا لما ادعاه أولا وآخرا من العلم واليقين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r1.claim: Some say Pharaoh denied a god only beyond his territory, believing whoever ruled a region was god to its inhabitants.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم في دفع ما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the contradiction escaped foolish people or they recognized it but feared Pharaoh; this allows literal uncertainty in ẓann.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r2.anchor: وفي الكشاف القول بالمناقضة بين بناء الصرح وما ادعاه من العلم واليقين إلا أنه قال قد خفيت على قومه لغباوتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī first prefers resolving the contradiction; failing that, he allows Pharaoh's ignorance or people's fear and foolishness.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r3.anchor: والاولى عندي السعي في دفع التناقض فاذا لم يكن استند في ارتكاب المخذول إياه إلى جهله

ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r4.speaker: القاضي البيضاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī al-Bayḍāwī says absent knowledge entails absence of its object for active knowledge, but not passive knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r4.anchor: وقال القاضي البيضاوي : هذا في العلوم الفعلية صحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r5.claim: Nonexistence can cause not knowing; customary implication supports this without strict logical entailment, making the phrase a metonymy for nonexistence.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r5.anchor: لما كان من أقوى أسباب عدم العلم لأنه المطرد جاز أن يطلق ويراد به الوجود

ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī treats the phrase as metonymy for denial of existence, not figurative substitution, and leaves the best reading to the reader.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p81#2/r6.anchor: ثم الظاهر أن الكلام على تقدير إرادة نفي الوجود كناية لا مجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r1.speaker: بعض من يقول إن الله تعالى في السماء
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r1.claim: Some proponents of God's being in heaven cite Pharaoh's request as proof Moses said so, alleging Pharaoh misunderstood it as bodily containment and a climbable location; al-Ālūsī calls it very weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r1.anchor: واستدل بعض من يقول : إن الله تعالى في السماء بالمعنى الذي أراده سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r2.claim: The phrase means firing clay, not making bricks; al-Ālūsī infers Pharaoh was teaching Hāmān, who apparently did not know brickmaking.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r2.anchor: والمراد به اللبن دون اصنع لي آجرا اشارة إلى أنه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r3.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir transmits Ibn Jurayj's report that Pharaoh was first to fire bricks and build with them.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r3.anchor: فقد أخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن جريج قال فرعون أول من طبخ الآجر

ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r4.speaker: عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r4.claim: When ʿUmar saw brick palaces in Syria, he said he knew of no builder in brick besides Pharaoh.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r4.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه حين سافر إلى الشام ورأى القصور المشيدة بالآجر

ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r5.claim: Pharaoh's bare address to Hāmān, order to do menial brick firing, and mid-sentence يا display arrogance.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p82/r5.anchor: وفي أمره إياه وهو وزيره ورديفه بعمل السفلة من الايقاد على الطين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r4.claim: The command means to fire bricks; one account says Pharaoh was the first to make and build with bricks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r4.anchor: فاطبخ لي الآجر، وقيل: إنه أول من اتخذ من الآجر وبنى به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r5.claim: A ṣarḥ is a high palace; another explanation is a tower or lighthouse.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r6.claim: Exegetes recount that Hāmān gathered fifty thousand builders plus crews, raised an unprecedented tower, and Pharaoh shot an arrow skyward that returned bloodied; he claimed to have killed Moses’ God, then Gabriel struck the tower apart, killing its workers and a million soldiers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r6.anchor: قال أهل التفسير (1) لما أمر فرعون وزيره هامان ببناء الصرح، جمع هامان العمال والفعلة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r7.claim: Pharaoh meant that he would look at Moses’ God and determine His condition.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r8.claim: The one Pharaoh calls a liar is Moses, for claiming that the earth and creation have a god other than Pharaoh and that he is God’s messenger.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p208#2/r8.anchor: يعني موسى، {من الكاذبين} في زعمه أن للأرض والخلق إلها غيري

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r1.claim: Pharaoh denies knowing another god, not that one exists: he had no basis for certainty about its nonexistence, so he orders the tower to investigate.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r1.anchor: نفى علمه بإله غيره دون وجوده إذ لم يكن عنده ما يقتضي الجزم بعدمه

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r2.claim: He imagines that any god would be a body in the sky that could be reached by climbing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r2.anchor: كأنه توهم أنه لو كان لكان جسما في السماء يمكن الترقي إليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r3.claim: Alternatively, he wanted an observatory to track celestial positions and learn whether they signaled a messenger's mission or a change of rule.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r3.anchor: أو أراد أن يبني له رصدا يترصد منه أوضاع الكواكب فيرى هل فيها ما يدل

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r4.claim: Pharaoh says that he thinks Moses is lying.

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r5.claim: A reported interpretation takes denial of knowledge as denial of the known, as in the verse meaning that there are no gods in the heavens or earth; this inference applies to active knowledge, whose objects depend on it, unlike passive knowledge.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد بنفي العلم نفي المعلوم

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r6.claim: A report calls Pharaoh the first to make fired brick; the order both teaches the craft and expresses grandeur, while the vocative يا Haman interrupts the sentence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:38-39/r6.anchor: قيل أول من اتخذ الآجر فرعون ولذلك أمر باتخاذه على وجه يتضمن تعليم الصنعة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh responds after Moses’ exhortations and warnings, once the great signs have been shown.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r1.anchor: جوابا لهذا الترغيب والترهيب بعد الإعذار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh’s recurring tactic is to keep his people from believing for a while whenever Moses shows a proof, exploiting their foolish preference for falsehood.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r2.anchor: كلما أظهر موسى عليه الصلاةوالسلام برهانا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r3.claim: He honors the nobles in his address to win their hearts.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r3.anchor: أي الأشراف , معظما لهم استجلابا لقلوبهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r4.claim: Pharaoh frames the denial as a lack of knowledge to appear fair, while using it to create doubt despite knowing Moses has the truth.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r4.anchor: إظهارا للنصفة , وأنه ما قصد غشهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r5.claim: Haman is Pharaoh’s minister, and the clay is made into bricks for building.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r6.claim: Pharaoh attributes the firing to himself to signal that it must be done.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r6.anchor: أضاف الإيقاد إليه إعلاما بأنه لا بد منه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r7.claim: A ṣarḥ is a tall structure that reaches toward the sky.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r7.anchor: { صرحا } اي بناء عايا يتاخم السماء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r8.speaker: الطبري
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r8.claim: Al-Tabari says every flat-roofed building is like a palace.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r8.anchor: قال الطبري : وكل بناء مسطح فهو كالقصر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r9.speaker: الزجاج
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines a ṣarḥ as any broad, elevated building.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج : كل بناء متسع مرتفع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r10.claim: Aṭṭaliʿ means that Pharaoh will undertake the effort of climbing.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r11.claim: Pharaoh pretends that he can seek Moses’ God in the sky if the claim is true, while being certain otherwise and using the project to delay belief.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r11.anchor: إله موسى } اي الذي يدعوا إليه , فإنه ليس في الرض أحد بهذا الوصف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r12.claim: The pronoun refers to Moses, whom Pharaoh accuses of being a habitual liar.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r12.anchor: أي موسى { من الكاذبين * } أي دأبه ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r13.claim: Taken literally, Pharaoh’s plan exposes his ignorance: he imagines reaching the sky, climbing it, and confronting its maker.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p489#2/r13.anchor: على حقيقته فلا شيء أثبت شهادة على غفراط جهله وغباوته

DURR-FULL:v6p415/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r1.speaker: الله تعالى
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r1.claim: The report links Pharaoh's claim to be the highest lord with a divine message to Gabriel that the servant had rebelled and his destruction had arrived.
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r1.anchor: فلما قال {أنا ربكم الأعلى} النازعات الآية 24 قال: يا جبريل قد سكنت روعتك بغى عبدي وقد جاء أوان هلاكه

DURR-FULL:v6p415/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports the Prophet saying Pharaoh made two claims, forty years apart, before God punished his later and earlier claim.
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كلمتان قالهما فرعون {ما علمت لكم من إله غيري} وقوله {أنا ربكم الأعلى}

DURR-FULL:v6p415/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r3.speaker: محدث حدثه
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r3.claim: An unnamed informant in Ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam's report says Haman was Nubian.
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r3.anchor: عن محدث حدثه قال: كان هامان نبطيا

DURR-FULL:v6p415/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r4.claim: Mujahid says the clay was molded and fired into bricks.
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين} قال على المدر يكون لبنا مطبوخا

DURR-FULL:v6p415/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r5.claim: Qatada says Pharaoh was the first to fire bricks and build the tower.
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r5.anchor: عن قتادة قال: كان فرعون أول من طبخ الآجر وصنع له الصرح

DURR-FULL:v6p415/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Pharaoh was the first to make bricks and build with them.
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: فرعون أول من صنع الآجر وبنى به

DURR-FULL:v6p415/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r7.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr says the clay was fired until it became brick.
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين} قال: اوقد على الطين حتى يكون آجرا

DURR-FULL:v6p415/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says after the tower was built Pharaoh climbed it, shot an arrow toward heaven, received it back bloodstained, and claimed he killed Moses's god.
DURR-FULL:v6p415/r8.anchor: عن السدي قال: لما بنوا له الصرح ارتقى فوقه فأمر بنشابة فرمى بها نحو السماء

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates that Gabriel asked God to destroy Pharaoh for claiming divinity. God said Pharaoh had an appointed term; after Pharaoh’s later claim to be the highest lord, Gabriel’s prior plea was recalled and Pharaoh ordered bricks fired.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قال : لما قال فرعون : ما علمت لكم من اله غيري قال جبريل عليه السلام : يا رب ، طغى عبدك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses the clay as mud fired into baked bricks.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : فاوقد لي يا هامان على الطين قال : على المدر ، يكون لبنا مطبوخا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r3.speaker: بلاغ غير مسمى
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r3.claim: An unnamed report says Pharaoh was the first to fire baked bricks.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r3.anchor: في قوله : اوقد لي يا هامان على الطين قال : بلغني ان اول من طبخ الاجر فرعون

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r4.claim: Qatāda says Pharaoh was the first to fire bricks and have a tower built for him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : فاوقد لي يا هامان على الطين إلى قوله : من الكاذبين قال : وكان اول من طبخ الاجر وصنع له الصرح

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the fired clay was building material; ṣarḥ means a building, which Pharaoh ordered raised.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r5.anchor: انبا عبد الرحمن بن زيد في قول الله فاوقد لي يا هامان على الطين قال : الطين المطبوخ

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says Pharaoh climbed the completed tower, shot an arrow skyward, received it back stained with blood, and claimed he had killed Moses’s God.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2978#3/r6.anchor: عن السدي قال : يا ايها الملأ ما علمت لكم من اله غيري فاوقد لي يا هامان على الطين فاجعل لي صرحا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r1.claim: This is a separate address to Pharaoh’s courtiers after his exchange with Moses, so the story is joined to the prior scene with a conjunction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r1.anchor: فهو كلام أقبل به على خطاب أهل مجلسه إثر المحاورة مع موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r2.claim: Pharaoh tries to secure his courtiers’ belief in his divinity and reject Moses’ teaching that God is Lord of their forefathers and of the heavens and earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r2.anchor: أراد فرعون بخطابه مع ملئه أن يثبتهم على عقيدة إلهيته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r3.claim: Denying that he knows of another god indirectly denies that one exists: Pharaoh pretends his knowledge covers all truth, so he would know of any rival.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r3.anchor: نفي وجود إله غيره بطريق الكناية يريهم أنه أحاط علمه بكل شيء حق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r4.claim: The god denied is Moses’ creator of all; the Egyptians’ supposed gods remain compatible with Pharaoh’s claim because they regarded him as their offspring and essence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r4.anchor: لأن فرعون عندهم هو مظهر الآلهة المزعومة عندهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r5.claim: Pharaoh misimagines the Lord of the heavens as residing in the sky, so he orders a tower to reach it and inspect for Moses’ God, claiming firsthand proof against Moses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r5.anchor: أن يبني له صرحا يبلغ به عنان السماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r6.claim: The staged search lets Pharaoh pose as a thorough seeker of truth, then use a supposed failed search to increase his courtiers’ confidence that Moses lied; the sophistry exposes their disordered and weak thinking.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p121/r6.anchor: وفي هذا الضغث من الجدل السفسطائي مبلغ من الدلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r1.claim: Haman is the title or name of Pharaoh’s minister.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r1.anchor: لقب أو اسم لوزير فرعون كما تقدم آنفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r2.claim: Kindling clay means ordering workers to fire clay into bricks; construction is expressed through its preliminary operation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r2.anchor: العملة أن يطبخوا الطين ليكون آجرا ويبنوا به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r3.claim: Pharaoh begins with the first construction task to start immediately: firing kilns to make bricks, whose base material is called clay.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r3.anchor: للدلالة على العناية بالشروع من أول أوقات الأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r4.claim: Brick rather than stone and lime allows a quickly raised tower; durability is irrelevant because it need only be seen before it is abandoned and demolished.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r4.anchor: قصدا للتعجيل بإقامة هذا الصرح المرتفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r5.speaker: ابن الأثير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r5.claim: Ibn al-Athir says clay replaces everyday terms for brick and tile because those words are too commonplace.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r5.anchor: قال ابن الأثير في ( المثل السائر ) :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r6.claim: The clearer reason for saying clay is that the word is lighter and more eloquent than the technical word for brick.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r6.anchor: وأظهر من كلام ابن الأثير : أن العدول إلى الطين لأنه أخف وأفصح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r7.claim: Attributing firing to Haman is figurative agency: he orders the work, as one says a ruler built a bridge or al-Mansur built Baghdad.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r8.claim: In earlier monarchies, royal commands passed through ministers, who implemented them using their officials and agents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r8.anchor: أوامر الملوك في العصور الماضية تصدر بواسطة الوزير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p122/r9.claim: Ṣarḥ means a high palace or elevated building.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r1.claim: Pharaoh’s hope of reaching heaven to find Moses’ God rests on false ideas that a tower can reach heaven and that God is located in a heavenly place.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r1.anchor: إذ حسب أن السماء يوصل إليها بمثل هذا الصرح ما طال بناؤه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r2.claim: Iṭṭilāʿ is forceful, effortful ascent undertaken because the task is difficult.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r3.claim: Ẓann here means certainty; Pharaoh’s attempt either strengthens that certainty or is meant to persuade his people.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r4.claim: Pharaoh may mislead his people into thinking Moses placed God at a reachable location, then treat not finding Him there as proof that He does not exist.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r4.anchor: ولعله أراد بهذا تمويه الأمر على قومه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r5.claim: The account portrays deviant beliefs as founded on false imaginings and their leaders’ deceptive arguments.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123/r5.anchor: وكانت دلائلها قائمة على تمويه الدجالين من زعمائهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r1.claim: Calling Moses one of the liars casts him as belonging to a group characterized by lying.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r1.anchor: يدل على أنه يعده من الطائفة الذين شأنهم الكذب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r2.claim: The Qur’an does not say whether the tower was built; it cannot be one of the pyramids, which were stone tombs rather than brick structures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r2.anchor: وليس هو أحد الأهرام لأن الأهرام بنيت من حجارة لا من آجر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r3.claim: One exegetical report says the tower was completed, Pharaoh climbed it, descended, and claimed he had killed Moses’ God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r3.anchor: فحكى بعضهم أنه تم وصعد فرعون إلى أعلاه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r4.claim: Another report says the unfinished tower collapsed, killing many builders and soldiers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r4.anchor: وحكى بعضهم أن الصرح سقط قبل إتمام بنائه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r5.claim: A third report says construction never began; the author postpones his own alternative reading to Sūrat Ghāfir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r5.anchor: وحكى بعضهم أنه لم يشرع في بنائه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r6.claim: The author notes that he will explain another possible meaning of the verse in Sūrat Ghāfir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p123#2/r6.anchor: وقد لاح لي في معنى الآية وجه آخر سأذكره في سورة المؤمن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r19.claim: Pharaoh continued his deception, ordering Hāmān to fire bricks and build a high-roofed structure to pretend he could see the sky.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r19.anchor: واستمر فرعون في طريق مخرقته على قومه وأمر هامان بأن يطبخ له الآجر وأن يبني له صرحا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r20.claim: A ṣarḥ is a raised structure with a roof or flat surface.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r20.anchor: أي سطحا في أعلى الهواء، وليس الصرح إلا ما له سطح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r21.claim: Firing over clay may refer to making tiles or bricks in molds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r21.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الإيقاد على الطين كالبرامي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r22.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r22.claim: Al-Suddī says Pharaoh built as high as possible and shot an arrow; God returned it bloodstained to deepen their blindness, then Pharaoh claimed to have killed Moses’ god.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r22.anchor: فروي عن السدي أنه بناه أعلى ما يمكن ثم صعد فيه ورمى بالنبل فردها الله تعالى إليه مخضوبة بالدم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r23.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r23.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r23.claim: Pharaoh means Moses lies about being sent by a sender; zann expresses settled disbelief and resolve to deny.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p287#3/r23.anchor: فالظن على بابه وهو معنى إيجاب الكفر بمنزلة التصميم على التكذيب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the command as making fired bricks.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة المعنى اصنع لي الآجر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines a sarh as a broad, tall building.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج الصرح كل بناء متسع مرتفع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r3.speaker: التفسير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r3.claim: A report says Haman gathered fifty thousand builders for an unprecedented tower. Pharaoh climbed it, shot an arrow skyward that returned bloodied, and claimed he had killed Moses' God; Gabriel broke the tower into three pieces, one killing a million soldiers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r3.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أنه لما أمر هامان وهو وزيره ببناء الصرح جمع العمال والفعلة حتى اجتمع خمسون ألف بناء سوى الأتباع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r4.claim: أطلع means to ascend and look out over something.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r5.speaker: author
