IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r5.claim: The pronoun means Moses, whom Pharaoh accuses of lying in claiming a god besides Pharaoh.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r5.anchor: في ادعائه إلها غيري وقال ابن جرير المعنى أظن موسى كاذبا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir says Pharaoh calls Moses a liar for claiming that a Lord in heaven sent him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p223/r6.anchor: وقال ابن جرير المعنى أظن موسى كاذبا في ادعائه أن في السماء ربا أرسله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238/r1.claim: Pharaoh's claim to divinity expresses his disbelief, tyranny, and false pretension; he demanded that his people acknowledge him as a god, and they obeyed foolishly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن كفر فرعون وطغيانه وافترائه في دعوى الإلهية لنفسه القبيحة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir links Pharaoh's public claim to his gathering and declaring himself the highest lord, which his people accepted, and God's making him a warning for later people.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238/r3.claim: Pharaoh had also threatened to imprison Moses if he worshipped a god other than Pharaoh.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238/r3.anchor: لئن اتخذت إلها غيري لأجعلنك من المسجونين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh orders his minister, administrator, and state adviser Haman to fire clay into bricks for construction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r1.anchor: أمر وزيره هامان ومدبر رعيته ومشير دولته أن يوقد له على الطين، ليتخذ له آجرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r2.claim: The ṣarḥ is a lofty, towering palace; another verse describes Pharaoh demanding a tower to reach the paths of the heavens.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r3.claim: Pharaoh built the tallest structure the world had seen to make his subjects think Moses' claim of a god besides Pharaoh was false.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r3.anchor: إنما أراد بهذا أن يظهر لرعيته تكذيب موسى فيما زعمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p238#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir's view, adopted here, is that Pharaoh called Moses a liar for claiming a god existed besides Pharaoh, not for claiming God had sent him; Pharaoh denied a creator, as shown by his questions and threats.

JISHUMI:v8p5501/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5501/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5501/r10.claim: Pharaoh claimed to be divine; another report says he also ordered idol worship and claimed to be the god of everyone.
JISHUMI:v8p5501/r10.anchor: تدل الآية على أنه كان يدعي الإلهية، وقيل: كان أيضا يأمر بعبادة الأوثان

JISHUMI:v8p5501/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5501/r11.speaker: المشبهة والكرامية
JISHUMI:v8p5501/r11.claim: Jishumi condemns the belief that Moses’ God is in heaven on the Throne, associating it with the anthropomorphists and Karramiyya whom the passage calls leaders of error.
JISHUMI:v8p5501/r11.anchor: وقد وافق في هذا الاعتقاد المشبهة والكرامية، واعتقدوا أنه في السماء على العرش

JISHUMI:v8p5501/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5501/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5501/r13.claim: Pharaoh probably knew he was not a god and had a creator, but he feigned doubt and persisted in defiance.
JISHUMI:v8p5501/r13.anchor: والأقرب أنه عرف من نفسه أنه ليس بإله، وأن له صانعا، ولكن لبس وعاند.

JISHUMI:v8p5501/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5501/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5501/r14.claim: Pharaoh contradicts himself by denying any god besides himself and then proposing to look for Moses’ God; Jishumi calls this typical of deviants and innovators.
JISHUMI:v8p5501/r14.anchor: وتدل على مناقضة في كلامه حيث يقول: (ما علمت لكم من إله غيري) ثم قال: (أطلع إلى إله موسى)، وهذا حال كل ضال ومبتدع.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p415#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p415#2/r6.speaker: ابن كثير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p415#2/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads قال موسى without واو, following the Meccan codices.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p415#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير : ( قال موسى ) بغير واو ، على ما في مصاحف أهل مكة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p415#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p415#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p415#2/r7.claim: The reading without واو suits a question about Moses' response when Pharaoh labels the signs sorcery or fabrication.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p415#2/r7.anchor: وهي قراءة حسنة ؛ لأن الموضع موضع سؤال وبحث عما أجابهم به موسى عليه السلام عند تسميتهم مثل تلك الآيات الباهرة : سحرا امفترى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p415#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p415#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p415#2/r8.claim: With واو, the statements are juxtaposed for comparison so an observer can see one is false and the other true; opposites clarify things.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p415#2/r8.anchor: ووجه الأخرى : أنهم قالوا ذلك . وقال موسى عليه السلام هذا ، ليوازن الناظر بين القول والمقول ، ويتبصر فساد أحدهما وصحة الآخر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r1.claim: A report says Hāmān assembled fifty thousand builders and workers to make brick, lime, timber, and nails for a tower higher than any before it; Gabriel broke it into three pieces, killing a million soldiers and the workers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r1.anchor: روى أنه لما أمر ببناء الصرح ، جمع هامان العمال حتى اجتمع خمسون ألف بناء سوى الأتباع والأجراء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r2.claim: A second report says Pharaoh climbed the tower and shot an arrow heavenward; it returned stained with blood, so he claimed to have killed Moses' god, after which Gabriel demolished the tower; al-Zamakhsharī questions its soundness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r2.anchor: أن فرعون ارتقى فوقه فرمى بنشابة نحو السماء ،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r3.claim: Pharaoh's claim that he knows no god but himself is intended to deny the existence of any other god, as in al-Aʿrāf 7:59.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r3.anchor: قصد بنفي علمه بإله غيره : نفي وجوده ، معناه : { ما لكم من إلاه * غيرى } ( الأعراف : 59 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r4.claim: The parallel question about informing God of what He does not know means there is nothing in heaven or earth; knowledge follows its object, so denial of knowledge expresses nonexistence.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r4.anchor: كما قال الله تعالى : { قل أتنبئون الله بما لا يعلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r5.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh literally means he knows of no other god; by calling Moses a liar without knowing him false, he implicitly supposes another god exists.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون على ظاهره ، وأن إلاها غيره غير معلوم عنده ، ولكنه مظنون بدليل قوله : { وإنى لاظنه من الكاذبين }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r6.claim: If Pharaoh knew Moses' claim false, he would not have built a tower to seek Moses' god; he instead imagined God as spatial, like himself.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r6.anchor: ولو لم يكن المخذول ظانا ظنا كاليقين ، بل عالما بصحة قول موسى عليه السلام لقول موسى له : { لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب * السماوات والأرض * بصائر }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r7.claim: The attempt to reach heaven with a tower displays the gross ignorance of Pharaoh and his nobles about God's nature and location.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r7.anchor: ولا ترى بينة أثبت شهادة على إفراط جهله وغباوته وجهل ملئه وغباوتهم : من أنهم راموا نيل أسباب السموات بصرح يبنون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r8.claim: The tower may have been Pharaoh's attempt to deceive a gullible people, or he may himself have been so foolish.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r8.anchor: أكان يلبس على أهل بلاده ويضحك من عقولهم ، حيث صادفهم أغبى الناس وأخلاهم من الفطن وأشبههم بالبهائم بذلك ؟

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r9.claim: If the arrow story is authentic, God mocked Pharaoh through the event, as the Qur'an mocks comparable unbelievers in speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r9.anchor: وإن صح ما حكى من رجوع النشابة إليه ملطوخة بالدم ، فتهكم به بالفعل ، كما جاء التهكم بالقول في غير موضع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r10.claim: Under the first explanation, ظن may mean certainty.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p417/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يفسر الظن على القول الأول باليقين ، كقوله :

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says forty years separated Pharaoh's claim of exclusive divinity from his later claim to be the highest lord.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كان بينها وبين قوله { أنا ربكم الأعلى } أربعون سنة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r2.claim: Qatada says Pharaoh was the first to fire bricks.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r2.anchor: قال قتادة : هو أول من طبخ الآجر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r3.claim: A ṣarḥ is a tall palace.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r3.anchor: فاجعل لي صرحا } الصرح القصر العالي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r4.claim: Qatada says Pharaoh was the first for whom a lofty structure was made.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r4.anchor: قال قتادة : هو أول من صنع له الصرح .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r5.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r5.claim: Al-Suddi relates that Pharaoh climbed the structure and shot an arrow toward heaven; it returned bloodied, and Pharaoh claimed he had killed Moses's god.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p253/r5.anchor: فحكى السدي أن فرعون صعد الصرح ورمى نشابه نحو السماء فرجعت إليه متلطخة دما

MUJAHID:v2p486#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p486#4/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
MUJAHID:v2p486#4/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains the command as firing clay or mud to make bricks.
MUJAHID:v2p486#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن المبارك عن ابن جريج في قوله ﴿ فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين ﴾ قال يعني على المدر

MUQATIL:28:38-42/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r1.claim: The assembly addressed by Pharaoh means the chiefs of his people.
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r1.anchor: { وقال فرعون يأيها الملأ } يعني الأشراف من قومه

MUQATIL:28:38-42/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r2.claim: Pharaoh’s claim that he knows no god for them except himself is an act of unbelief.
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r2.anchor: { ما علمت لكم من إله غيري } هذا القول من فرعون كفر

MUQATIL:28:38-42/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r3.claim: Haman was to fire clay into bricks; Pharaoh was the first to bake bricks and build with them.
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r3.anchor: يقول: أوقد النار على الطين حتى يصير اللبن أجرا

MUQATIL:28:38-42/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r4.claim: A ṣarḥ is a tall palace; its mortar was glass slag, and the wind made it frightening to stand on lest a person be swept away.
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r4.anchor: ملاطه خبث القوارير، فكان الرجل لا يستطيع القيام عليه

MUQATIL:28:38-42/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r5.claim: Pharaoh wanted to look for Moses’s God and claimed Moses was lying when he said God was in heaven.
MUQATIL:28:38-42/r5.anchor: بما يقول: إن في السماء إلها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh's denial of knowing another god can imply that no other god exists for them, or be taken literally as saying no other god is known to him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r1.anchor: قصد بنفي علمه باله غيره نفى وجوده أي مالكم من إله غيري أو هو على ظاهره

NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r2.claim: He asks Haman to bake clay into bricks and build with them; this phrasing is apt because Pharaoh is said to be the first brickmaker and it teaches the craft.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r2.anchor: أي اطبخ لي الآجر واتخذه وأنما لم يقل مكان الطين هذا لأنه أول من عمل الآجر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r3.claim: Calling Haman by name in the middle of the command, and ordering him to fire the clay, sounds eloquent and tyrannical, signaling Pharaoh's arrogance.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r3.anchor: ولأنه أفصح وأشبه بكلام الجبابرة إذ أمر هامان وهو وزيره بالايقاد على الطين منادي باسمه بيافي وسط الكلام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r4.claim: A ṣarḥ is a high palace or building.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r5.claim: Aṭṭaliʿ means to ascend; iṭṭilāʿ is climbing upward.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r6.claim: Pharaoh imagined that God occupied a place, as Pharaoh himself did.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r6.anchor: حسب أنه تعالى في مكان كما كان هو في مكان

NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r7.claim: Pharaoh calls Moses a liar for claiming to have a god who sent him as a messenger.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r7.anchor: في دعواه أن له إلها وأنه أرسله إلينا رسولا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r8.claim: Pharaoh contradicts himself: he first denies any god but himself, then asks Haman for help and admits Moses has a god, while conceding he is not certain Moses lies.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r8.anchor: وقد تناقض المخذول فإنه قال ما علمت لكم من إله غيري ثم أظهر حاجته إلى هامان وأثبت لموسى إلها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r9.claim: An anonymous report says Haman gathered fifty thousand builders for an unprecedented tower; Gabriel struck it apart, killing a million of Pharaoh's soldiers with one section, while the others fell into the sea and west, and every worker died.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p237#2/r9.anchor: روى أن هامان جمع خمسين ألف بناء وبنى صرحا لم يبلغه بناء أحد من الخلق فضرب الصرح جبريل عليه السلام بجناحه

QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says forty years separated Pharaoh's claim here from أنا ربكم الأعلى; Pharaoh lied, for he knew he had a Lord who created him and his people, as 43:87 confirms.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان بينها وبين قوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the command as cooking bricks for Pharaoh.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r9.anchor: أي اطبخ لي الآجر عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r10.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r10.claim: Qatada says Pharaoh was the first to make fired bricks and build with them.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو أول من صنع الآجر وبنى به

QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r11.claim: Haman gathered fifty thousand builders, apart from support workers, and ordered bricks and plaster baked, timber cut, and nails made; the structure rose beyond any previous building.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r11.anchor: جمع هامان العمال قيل خمسين ألف بناء سوى الأتباع والأجراء

QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r12.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r12.claim: Al-Suddi says Pharaoh climbed the structure and shot an arrow skyward; when it returned stained with blood, Pharaoh claimed to have killed Moses' god.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r12.anchor: فحكى السدي: أن فرعون صعد السطح ورمى بنشابة نحو السماء

QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r13.claim: A report says Gabriel struck the tower with his wing, splitting it into three pieces that fell on the army, into the sea, and westward; the author questions the report's reliability.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r13.anchor: فروي أن جبريل عليه السلام بعثه الله تعالى عند مقالته، فضرب الصرح بجناحه

QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r14.claim: ظن here means doubt; Pharaoh disbelieved while doubting, despite proofs so evident that a sound nature would not be deceived by them.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:36-40/r14.anchor: الظن هنا شك، فكفر على الشك لأنه قد رأى من البراهين ما لا يخيل على ذي فطرة

BURHAN:v1p434/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p434/r5.speaker: سفيان الثوري
BURHAN:v1p434/r5.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri reportedly wrote a charm for a divorced woman to wear over her heart, using verses about the sky and earth opening and Pharaoh emerging.
BURHAN:v1p434/r5.anchor: وكان سفيان الثورى يكتب للمطلقة رقعة تعلق على قلبها
